correctness.rationale: The code phi(a)=001 h(e(a)) 10 is injective and synchronized because 001 occurs only at aligned starts; with g=1^k, first/last-bit arguments exclude codewords from every g t g penalty word, and encoded strings avoid 1^k. These are exactly the hypotheses of the published synchronized-code reduction. NP membership follows by direct verification of a trigger-set certificate.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The motivating 2026 paper proves alphabet-size-three hardness and does not state a binary result. Searches for binary MPFG/prefix-free-graph hardness and equivalent trigger-selection formulations, plus the current SCOPE archive check, found no prior coverage. The source is recent, so near-simultaneous or revision risk remains.

value.rationale: The result closes the alphabet-size hardness gap at the minimum nontrivial alphabet. It also identifies a useful complexity contrast: every fixed trigger length is polynomial over a binary alphabet by the existing O(2^q N) algorithm, whereas NP-completeness already holds for logarithmic trigger length.
